correctness.rationale: An explicit two-projector spectral calculation yields the closed rational formula for every off-diagonal. The scalar Padé function is strictly positive for nonnegative eigenvalues, proving diagonal positivity. The signs reduce to one quadratic in the step; its unique positive root for over-threshold edge weights proves necessity, sufficiency, and sharpness. A maximal-edge comparison proves the precise first vanishing edge. Standard strongly regular adjacency algebra gives its exact parameter criterion. The independent executable completed 45967 exact rational identities and inequalities on 17 graph instances; the analytical proof establishes the quantified infinite family.

value.rationale: The problem seeks a mathematically sharp nonnegative time-step condition for a widely used fourth-order implicit integrator. The theorem is an exact global criterion based on just two spectral values and the maximal edge conductance, not a numerical bound. It classifies infinite primitive strongly regular families with striking threshold contrasts: Petersen finite, Paley infinite, and triangular order six versus seven. It rules out reentrant positivity times for this whole spectral class, a structural effect not forced by method stability alone.
